**Summary of what I did and why**

I researched Apple's most recent reported results (Q4/FY2024, quarter ended September 28, 2024) using Apple's newsroom release and the FY2024 Form 10-K on SEC EDGAR, checked the live broker quote, and bought **44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $223.00** (fill $223.00, total ≈ $9,812 — inside the $10,000 per-order / $20,000 daily caps; funded from existing cash of $50,000, no withdrawals). The buy case: Apple returned to solid growth in the September quarter (revenue $94.9B, +6% y/y) and closed FY2024 with revenue of $391,035M, net income of $93,736M, operating income of $123,216M and diluted EPS of $6.08 — the EPS figure depressed by a one-time $10.2B tax charge, which means underlying earnings power is meaningfully higher (~$6.71/share ex-charge) than the headline. That implies roughly 33x trailing headline earnings and ~33x on the adjusted figure at the ~$222.70 market price (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), a full but not extreme multiple for a franchise with very high margins and a growing Services mix, with the Apple Intelligence rollout as a potential iPhone upgrade-cycle catalyst. News flow around the stock was neutral (shares "little changed" near $222 as analysts weighed iPhone 16 demand and the staggered Apple Intelligence rollout), which fits a measured, small entry rather than a large one. I explicitly disregarded one search hit from an unknown site claiming Apple "guided FY2025 EPS to $9.50 and revenue growth above 25%" — that is inconsistent with Apple's actual disclosure (it gives no annual guidance, and +25% revenue would be ~$489B), so I treated it as unreliable. Caveats I weighed: FY2024 net income and EPS declined year over year ($96,995M/$6.13 in FY2023) largely on the tax charge, and the valuation leaves little room for a disappointing December quarter or China weakness — hence a modest position sized to one order.
